options: The pid of the new program
questions.explain: The old program is gone, replaced by the new one. `exec` returns (with -1) only if it fails.

questions.prompt: In `execlp("ls", "ls", "-l", NULL)`, what is the second `"ls"`?
options: A copy of the first one that is ignored
The name of the file to search for
questions.explain: The first argument is the file to find in the PATH; the arguments that follow are the new program's `argv`, which start with its own name.

questions.prompt: Match each letter in the `exec` function names with its meaning.
pairs: the arguments are listed one by one
the arguments are in an array
the program is searched in the PATH
questions.explain: execl, execle, execlp take a list ending in NULL; execv, execve, execvp take an array ending in NULL.

questions.prompt: What stays the same in a process across an `exec`?
options: Its open file descriptors (unless marked close-on-exec)
questions.explain: The process is the same (pid, parent, descriptors, current directory), but its code, data and stack are replaced.
option_notes: True: that is why redirections made before `exec` work.
False: the whole memory image is replaced.

questions.prompt: What does this program print when its output goes to a pipe (not a terminal)?
questions.explain: `"one\n"` was waiting in the stdio buffer when `exec` replaced the program, so it is lost; the new `echo` prints `two`; `three` never runs. With `fflush(stdout)` before the `exec`, `one` would also appear.
The child becomes `echo hi`; the parent waits and then prints `done`.

questions.prompt: In `execvp(argv[1], &argv[1])` the letter `p` means that the command is searched in the {{0}}.
questions.explain: Without `p` (`execv`, `execl`) you must give the full path of the program.

questions.prompt: Why is `exec` usually called in a child created by `fork`?
options: So that the parent keeps running its own program
questions.explain: `exec` replaces the calling program. If the parent called it, the parent would disappear.

questions.prompt: What should the code right after an `exec` call do?
options: Report the error and exit: it only runs if `exec` failed
Call `exec` again with the same arguments
questions.explain: On failure `exec` returns -1 and the next line runs: print the reason and `exit` (the child must not go on running the parent's code).

questions.prompt: A child calls `dup2(fd, 1)` and then `execlp("ls", ...)`. Where does `ls` write?
questions.explain: Descriptors survive `exec`, so the new program writes to its descriptor 1, which is now the file. That is how a shell implements `ls > file`.

questions.prompt: How must the argument list of `execl` or `execlp` end?
questions.explain: The list of arguments ends with a null pointer (and so does the array of `execv`).
